checkpoint_review: The Router was generally rigorous but slightly too strict on the 'rectangular slab' checkpoint. While technically a clamshell is not a slab, it is a valid form factor for 'hand-held computer'. However, marking it false is acceptable given the strict taxonomy prior. The Router correctly identified the screen content as missing/blank (is_present: false). The untestable checkpoints (ports, weight) were handled correctly. I agree with all verdicts.
artifact_review: The Router identified text gibberish on the keyboard (severity 2.5), which is confirmed by the Image Text Auditor returning empty blocks (total failure to render legible text). The Router noted hinge structural collapse (severity 1.5); while the Topology Auditor gave a high confidence mask, this only confirms the object is segmented, not that the internal mechanics are correct. The hinge does look fused/melted upon visual inspection. The perspective distortion (severity 1.0) is minor. I agree with the severities; the text issue is the most significant artifact.
alignment_reasoning: The Fine Grained Classifier strongly confirms the class (Top-1 logit 7.23). The device has the core components (screen, keyboard) but fails the specific 'slab' geometry prior and lacks visible OS interface/text. It is clearly a hand-held computer, but deviates from the specific textual description provided in the taxonomy.
artifact_reasoning: Major artifact: Keyboard legends are completely illegible/gibberish (confirmed by OCR failure). Moderate artifact: Hinge mechanism is structurally vague/fused. Minor artifact: Slight perspective warping on key rows. The image is coherent but lacks the fine-grained textual fidelity expected of a manufactured object.
